newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam puts 1996 trade deficit at record $4.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam puts 1996 trade deficit at record $4.0 bln.

text.p: Vietnam's trade deficit rose to a record $4.0 billion in 1996 from $2.2 billion last year due to a surge in imports, the government's General Statistics Office said on Monday.
The statistics office's estimates put exports for the whole year at $7.1 billion, up 30 percent from 1995, and imports up 36 percent at $11.1 billion.

The country's trade deficit -- spawned by the fast-growing economy's voracious appetite for imports of capital goods and, increasingly, consumer goods -- has emerged as one of the government's chief economic problems over the past year.
A trade deficit of $4.0 billion would be equivalent to around 18 percent of the country's gross domestic product (GDP).

Minister of Planning and Investment Tran Xuan Gia said at the weekend that 1996 had been another year of vigorous economic growth, with GDP rising by 9.5 percent, but warned that the trade gap urgently needed to be tackled.

"If this is not solved, it will lead to the collapse of our trade and payment balance in coming years," he wrote in the Vietnam Investment Review, adding that import management was slack and illegal imports were still a serious problem.
